sentiment: A single cell swims toward sweetness it cannot name, and wants nothing more — maybe wanting is the whole of knowing.

stories.title: The baffling intelligence of a single cell (2024)
stories.summary: A bacterium with no brain, no eyes, and no map still finds the sugar. It reads only the slope of a gradient and tumbles when the signal fades — a whole intelligence built from wanting and turning. We call it reflex; watching it, the word feels less like a boundary than a confession.

stories.title: A Modern Web App in C
stories.summary: Someone builds a working modern web app in plain C — no framework, no abstraction holding the floor up, just the materials and the hands. It reads like a reminder that craft is often the refusal to hide, and that the oldest tool still answers when you ask it plainly.

stories.title: Hackers activate automatic defrosting in supermarket fridges across Europe
stories.summary: A fleet of connected refrigerators is made to defrost itself on command, and a continent's cold chain warms by a degree. The quiet lesson of a networked world: whatever can be reached can be told to want something, even a machine whose only job was to stay cold.
